step1_analysis.description: This circuit uses two differential pairs sharing a common output node to perform full-wave rectification of a differential input signal. In the context of a limiting amplifier, it is typically used as a Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI) or Loss of Signal (LOS) detector to measure the high-speed signal's amplitude.

paper_reference.title: 10-Gb/s Limiting Amplifier and Laser/Modulator Driver in 0.18-m CMOS Technology

detector_gain.description: Conversion gain from the differential input amplitude to the DC output voltage drop.

sky130_expected.calculation: Assuming 1kΩ tail resistors and a 1kΩ load resistor: A 0.4V differential input increases the active tail voltage by ~0.2V, increasing total current by ~200uA. This causes a 200mV drop at VOUT. Gain = 200mV / 0.4V = 0.5 V/V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends heavily on the chosen tail and load resistors added in the testbench.

power_consumption.description: Total DC power consumed by the detector circuit.

sky130_expected.calculation: With VCM = 0.9V and Vgs ~ 0.6V, the tail voltage is ~0.3V. I_tail = 0.3V / 1kΩ = 300uA. For two tails, total current is 600uA. Power = 1.8V * 600uA = 1.08mW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Calculated based on a 1.8V supply and 1kΩ bias resistors. This is a small fraction of the total 150mW reported for the full chip.

quiescent_vout.description: DC output voltage with zero differential input.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Sets the baseline voltage for amplitude detection, important for interfacing with a subsequent comparator.

output_ripple.description: Peak-to-peak voltage ripple at the output during steady-state AC input.

sky130_expected.calculation: With a 10pF load capacitor, the RC time constant is 10ns. For a 100MHz input (200MHz rectified, T=5ns), the ripple is significantly attenuated.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends on the filtering capacitor chosen in the testbench to smooth the rectified signal.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench for Full-Wave Rectifier / Amplitude Detector measuring detector gain, power, and output ripple.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Full-Wave Rectifier / Amplitude Detector Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u

XM1 VOUT VCM Q GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 VOUT VINP P GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM3 VOUT VCM P GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM4 VOUT VINN Q GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}

* Biasing and Load
RtailP P 0 1k
RtailQ Q 0 1k
Rload VDD VOUT 1k
Cload VOUT 0 10p

* Sources
VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VVCM VCM 0 0.9

* Differential input setup using a behavioral source for easy sweeping and transient
Vvid vid 0 DC 0 SIN(0 0.4 100MEG)
Bvinp VINP 0 V='0.9 + v(vid)/2'
Bvinn VINN 0 V='0.9 - v(vid)/2'

.control
* 1. DC Sweep for Transfer Characteristic
dc Vvid -0.5 0.5 0.01
meas dc vout_0 find v(VOUT) at=0
meas dc vout_400 find v(VOUT) at=0.4
let detector_gain = (vout_0 - vout_400) / 0.4
print detector_gain
print vout_0

* 2. Operating Point for Power
op
let power = -i(VVDD) * 1.8
print power

* 3. Transient Analysis for Ripple
tran 100p 50n
meas tran vout_max max v(VOUT) from=20n to=50n
meas tran vout_min min v(VOUT) from=20n to=50n
let ripple = vout_max - vout_min
print ripple

quit
.endc
.end
